ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p32/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p32/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p32/r2.claim: The arrogant Quraysh leader fashioned a disdainfully delivered excuse, misjudging the Qur’an as a prophet’s stirring eloquence and ignoring its warning, though its statements are realities he will soon meet.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p32/r2.anchor: they reckoned it to be a miracle of a prophet’s stirring and eloquent speech and never paid attention to its warning

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p45/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p45/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p45/r4.claim: He calls the Qur'an magic and human speech; Quraysh used the magic label as propaganda after they could no longer deny its eloquence and force.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p45/r4.anchor: they embarked upon a propaganda campaign against it

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p45/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p45/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p45/r5.claim: By calling it inherited magic, opponents claimed its spellbinding effect was merely human and familiar from earlier poets and orators, not divine or unique.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p45/r5.anchor: It was something which existed from previous times

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p329#2/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p329#2/r1.speaker: غير مسمى
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p329#2/r1.claim: In the reported debate, al-Walīd concedes that the people have never known Muhammad to lie, then calls the Qurʾān sorcery because it divides a man from his family and companions, alleging it was taken from Musaylima or Babylon.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p329#2/r1.anchor: وتزعمون أنه كذب، فهل جربتم عليه شيئا من الكذب؟

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p329#2/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p329#2/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p329#2/r2.claim: A second report says al-Walīd admired the Qurʾān repeatedly and came close to Islam, but Abū Jahl pressured him with claims that Quraysh suspected his visits to Abū Bakr and would accept him only if he condemned the message.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p329#2/r2.anchor: وروي أن الوليد سمع من القرآن ما أعجبه ومدحه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p330/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p330/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p330/r4.claim: The conjunctions distinguish related acts: frowning and scowling are near-synonyms, arrogance causes turning away, while the fāʾ signals his immediate utterance after forming the charge.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p330/r4.anchor: وكان العطف في وبسر وفي واستكبر، لأن البسور قريب من العبوس

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p330/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p330/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p330/r5.claim: The verb يؤثر means either is transmitted and repeated or is chosen and preferred, with poetry cited for the transmitted sense; إلا سحر means something resembling sorcery.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p330/r5.anchor: ومعنى يؤثر: يروى وينقل، قال الشاعر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p330/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p330/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p330/r7.claim: Abū Ḥayyān links al-Walīd's rejection to his encounter with the opening of Fussilat, where he pleaded with Muhammad to stop at the warning of ʿĀd and Thamūd.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p330/r7.anchor: وقصته مع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم حين قرأ عليه أوائل سورة فصلت

ASAD-NOTES:74:16#n12/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:74:16#n12/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:74:16#n12/r1.claim: Sihr usually means sorcery or magic; its primary sense is changing something from its proper or natural state, as Taj al-'Arus explains.
ASAD-NOTES:74:16#n12/r1.anchor: the turning of something from its proper [or "natural"] state of being into another state

ASAD-NOTES:74:16#n12/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:74:16#n12/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:74:16#n12/r2.claim: Sihr can describe the fascination or enchantment produced by exceptional, spellbinding eloquence.
ASAD-NOTES:74:16#n12/r2.anchor: often applied to the fascination or enchantment caused by exceptional, "spellbinding" eloquence

ASAD-NOTES:74:16#n12/r3.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:74:16#n12/r3.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:74:16#n12/r3.claim: When deniers use sihr for a divine message, it also implies deliberate deception or delusion.
ASAD-NOTES:74:16#n12/r3.anchor: used by deniers of the truth to describe a divine message - it has also the connotation of wilful deception

ALUSI-FULL:v29p124#5/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p124#5/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p124#5/r1.claim: The preferred sense of “transmitted” is that the statement is retold and learned from the magic of Babylon and similar sources.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p124#5/r1.anchor: أي يروى ويتعلم من سحر بابل ونحوهم

ALUSI-FULL:v29p124#5/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p124#5/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p124#5/r2.claim: A further proposed sense is “chosen and preferred over other magic,” but al-Ālūsī says it is not the selected interpretation.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p124#5/r2.anchor: وقيل أي يختار ويرجح على غيره من السحر وليس بمختار

ALUSI-FULL:v29p124#5/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p124#5/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p124#5/r3.claim: The fa shows that once the foolish phrase occurred to him he uttered it immediately, without pause or hesitation; this does not conflict with the earlier report.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p124#5/r3.anchor: والفاء للدلالة على أن هذه الكلمة الحمقاء لما خطرت بباله تفوه بها من غير تلثم وتلبث

BIQAI-FULL:v8p227/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p227/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p227/r9.claim: His allegation treats Muhammad’s message as only an illusory set of effects without reality, whose causes are too subtle to see.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p227/r9.anchor: أمور تخييلية لا حقائق لها , وهي لدقتها بحيث تخفى أسبابها

BIQAI-FULL:v8p227/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p227/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p227/r10.claim: He made the charge after his corrupt nature led him to think it useful in worldly life, without considering God’s judgment or the Hereafter.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p227/r10.anchor: لكونه رآه نافعا لهم في الدنيا ولم يفكر في عاقبة ذلك من جهة الله

BIQAI-FULL:v8p227/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p227/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p227/r11.claim: Yuʾthar means that a listener transmits it from another; the alleged magic is said to spread powerfully and divide spouses and close relatives.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p227/r11.anchor: من شأنه أن ينقله السامع له من غيره , فهو لقوة سحريته وإفراطها في بابها يفرق بمجرد الرواية

BIQAI-FULL:v8p227/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p227/r12.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p227/r12.claim: The charge is transparently false on reflection because Muhammad had never practiced magic or learned it.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p227/r12.anchor: محمدا صلى الله عليه وسلم ما سحر قط ولا تعلم سحرا , فكان من ادعى ذلك علم كذبه بأدنى نظر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p306/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p306/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p306/r10.claim: The worldly threat follows his worldly motives of leadership and envy; the threat of Hell follows his attacks on the Qur’an and denial of revelation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p306/r10.anchor: وقد وزع وعيده على ما تقتضيه أعماله فإنه لما ذكر عناده وهو من مقاصده السيئة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p309#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p309#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p309#2/r8.claim: The exclusive wording presents magic as the conclusion of his testing and sorting through possible descriptions of the Qur’an.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p309#2/r8.anchor: مشعرة بأن استقراء أحوال القرآن بعد السبر والتقسيم أنتج له أنه من قبيل السحر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p309#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p309#2/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p309#2/r9.claim: Maʾthūr means transmitted from ancient people; he calls the magic inherited to answer the objection that its language and effects resemble neither familiar magic nor the Prophet’s state.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p309#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p309#2/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p309#2/r10.claim: He alleges that the Qur’an consists of unfamiliar magical sayings to explain its difference from ordinary spells and the Prophet’s circumstances.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p309#2/r10.anchor: فزعم أنه أقوال سحرية غير مألوفة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p407#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p407#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p407#2/r1.claim: He claimed that the Quran was only sorcery transmitted from sorcerers.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p407#2/r1.anchor: فقال إن هذا أي ما هذا القرآن إلا سحر يؤثر أي يروى عن السحرة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p266/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p266/r7.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p266/r7.claim: He claimed Muhammad transmitted this magic from those before him.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p266/r7.anchor: أي: هذا سحر ينقله محمد عن غيره عمن قبله ويحكيه عنهم؛

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p266/r9.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p266/r9.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p266/r9.claim: The man is al-Walid ibn al-Mughira al-Makhzumi, a Quraysh leader.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p266/r9.anchor: وهذا المذكور في هذا السياق هو: الوليد بن المغيرة المخزومي، أحد رؤساء قريش

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p266/r10.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p266/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p266/r10.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that al-Walid first praised the Quran as neither poetry, magic, nor madness but God’s speech; after Abu Jahl’s pressure he called it transmitted magic.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p266/r10.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: دخل الوليد بن المغيرة على أبي بكر بن أبي قحافة فسأله

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p267/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p267/r2.speaker: عكرمة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p267/r2.claim: Ikrima reports al-Walid softened on hearing Muhammad recite; Abu Jahl manipulated him into denouncing it, and he eventually called it learned magic.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p267/r2.anchor: عن عكرمة: أن الوليد بن المغيرة جاء إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقرأ عليه القرآن، فكأنه رق له.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p267/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p267/r3.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p267/r3.claim: Ibn Ishaq and other historians report a similar account.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p267/r3.anchor: وقد ذكر محمد بن إسحاق وغير واحد نحوا من هذا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p267/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p267/r4.speaker: السدي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p267/r4.claim: Al-Suddi says Quraysh’s council debated calling Muhammad poet, magician, soothsayer, or madman to deter pilgrims; al-Walid then chose the charge of transmitted magic.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p267/r4.anchor: وقد زعم السدي أنهم لما اجتمعوا في دار الندوة ليجمعوا رأيهم على قول يقولونه فيه، قبل أن يقدم عليهم وفود العرب للحج

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p267/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p267/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p267/r5.claim: The Quran elsewhere describes these disbelievers as inventing comparisons and losing the way.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p267/r5.anchor: كما قال تعالى: {انظر كيف ضربوا لك الأمثال فضلوا فلا يستطيعون سبيلا}

NASAFI-FULL:v4p295#13/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p295#13/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p295#13/r1.claim: He called the Qurʾān magic passed down from sorcerers.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p295#13/r1.anchor: ﴿ فقال إن هذا ﴾ ما هذا ﴿ إلا سحر يؤثر ﴾ يروى عن السحرى

NASAFI-FULL:v4p295#13/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p295#13/r2.speaker: الوليد
NASAFI-FULL:v4p295#13/r2.claim: Al-Walīd first praised Muḥammad's speech as sweet, beautiful, fruitful, and surpassing human and jinn speech; after Abū Jahl pressured him, he rejected claims that Muḥammad was mad, a soothsayer, poet, or liar, then called the Qurʾān sorcery that divides families and is inherited from Musaylima and Babylonian sorcerers.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p295#13/r2.anchor: روى أن الوليد قال لبني مخزوم والله لقد سمعت من محمد آنفا كلاما ما هو من كلام الانس ولا من كلام الجن

NASAFI-FULL:v4p295#13/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p295#13/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p295#13/r3.claim: The fāʾ shows that as soon as the accusation occurred to him, he said it without hesitation.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p295#13/r3.anchor: وذكر الفاء دليل على أن هذه الكلمة لما خطرت بباله نطق بها من غير تلبث

QURTUBI-FULL:74:23-25/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:74:23-25/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:74:23-25/r9.claim: Al-Walid claims that Muhammad's message is transmitted magic; sihr here means deception.
QURTUBI-FULL:74:23-25/r9.anchor: { فقال إن هذآ } أي ما هذا الذي أتي به محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم { إلا سحر يؤثر } أي يأثره عن غيره. والسحر: الخديعة.

QURTUBI-FULL:74:23-25/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:74:23-25/r10.speaker: قوم
QURTUBI-FULL:74:23-25/r10.claim: Some define magic as making falsehood appear in the form of truth.
QURTUBI-FULL:74:23-25/r10.anchor: وقال قوم: السحر: إظهار الباطل في صورة الحق.

QURTUBI-FULL:74:23-25/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:74:23-25/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:74:23-25/r11.claim: Athara is the verbal noun of athartu al-hadith, to recount something from another; a ma'thur report is transmitted from earlier generations.
QURTUBI-FULL:74:23-25/r11.anchor: والأثره: مصدر قولك: أثرت الحديث آثره إذا ذكرته عن غيرك ومنه قيل: حديث مأثور: أي ينقله خلف عن سلف

QURTUBI-FULL:74:23-25/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:74:23-25/r12.speaker: امرؤ القيس
QURTUBI-FULL:74:23-25/r12.claim: Imru al-Qays's verse uses yuʾtharu for something that continues to be recounted until the end of time.
QURTUBI-FULL:74:23-25/r12.anchor: قال امرؤ القيس: ولو عن نثا غيره جاءني وجرح اللسان كجرح اليد

QURTUBI-FULL:74:23-25/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:74:23-25/r13.speaker: الأعشى
QURTUBI-FULL:74:23-25/r13.claim: Al-Aʿsha's verse witnesses the word al-athir for a hearer or transmitter.
QURTUBI-FULL:74:23-25/r13.anchor: وقال الأعشى: إن الذي فيه تماريتما بين للسامع والآثر

RAZI-FULL:v30p178/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p178/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p178/r2.claim: The fāʾ marks immediate sequence: after turning away in pride, he voiced this objection.
RAZI-FULL:v30p178/r2.anchor: وإنما ذكره بفاء التعقيب ليعلم أنه لما ولى واستكبر ذكر هذه الشبهة

RAZI-FULL:v30p178/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p178/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p178/r3.claim: One sense is that the magic is related as a story passed down from earlier people; the root usage is reporting after them.
RAZI-FULL:v30p178/r3.anchor: أثرت الحديث آثره أثرا إذا حدثت به عن قوم في آثارهم ، أي بعدما ماتوا

RAZI-FULL:v30p178/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p178/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p178/r4.claim: Alternatively, it means that this is preferred above all magic, from the verb for preferring one thing over another.
RAZI-FULL:v30p178/r4.anchor: الثاني : يؤثر على جميع السحر ، وعلى هذا يكون هو من الإيثار

TAB-FULL:v23p428/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p428/r3.speaker: عكرمة
TAB-FULL:v23p428/r3.claim: Ikrima recounts that al-Walid ibn al-Mughira was moved by Muhammad's recitation and praised its sweetness and force, but after Abu Jahl pressured him to oppose it he decided to call it magic inherited from another; the passage was revealed.
TAB-FULL:v23p428/r3.anchor: عن عكرمة أن الوليد بن المغيرة جاء إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم، فقرأ عليه القرآن، فكأنه رق له

TAB-FULL:v23p428/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p428/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v23p428/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that al-Walid first told Quraysh the Qur'an was God's speech, not poetry, magic, or madness; fearing his conversion, Abu Jahl shamed him into calling it magic acquired from others, and the passage was revealed.
TAB-FULL:v23p428/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: {إنه فكر وقدر} [المدثر: 18] إلى {ثم عبس وبسر} [المدثر: 22] قال: دخل الوليد بن المغيرة على أبي بكر

TAB-FULL:v23p431/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p431/r3.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v23p431/r3.claim: Al-Dahhak identifies the solitary one as al-Walid, whom Muhammad invited to Islam; after delaying, considering, frowning, turning away, and calling the message magic, he was consigned to Saqar.
TAB-FULL:v23p431/r3.anchor: سمعت الضحاك، يقول في قوله: {ذرني ومن خلقت وحيدا} [المدثر: 11] يعني الوليد بن المغيرة دعاه نبي الله

TAB-FULL:v23p431/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p431/r4.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v23p431/r4.claim: Ibn Zayd recounts that al-Walid examined Muhammad reciting in prayer, called the speech sweet and heart-gripping, rejected poetry and soothsaying, then allowed that it might be magic transmitted from earlier people.
TAB-FULL:v23p431/r4.anchor: قال ابن زيد في قوله: {ذرني ومن خلقت وحيدا وجعلت له مالا ممدودا} [المدثر: 12] إلى قوله

TAB-FULL:v23p432/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p432/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v23p432/r1.claim: He turned away from faith and belief in God's revelation, arrogantly refusing the truth; he claimed the Qur'an was magic taken from another person.
TAB-FULL:v23p432/r1.anchor: ثم ولى عن الإيمان والتصديق بما أنزل الله من كتابه، واستكبر عن الإقرار بالحق

TAB-FULL:v23p432/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p432/r2.speaker: أبو رزين
TAB-FULL:v23p432/r2.claim: Abu Razin glosses yuʾtharu as taking or receiving the magic from someone else.
TAB-FULL:v23p432/r2.anchor: عن أبي رزين، {إن هذا إلا سحر يؤثر} [المدثر: 24] قال: يأخذه عن غيره

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p430/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p430/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p430/r4.claim: The demonstrative refers to the Qur’an.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p430/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p430/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p430/r5.claim: The accusation was that Muhammad took this magic from Musaylima and transmitted it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p430/r5.anchor: {إلا سحر يؤثر}، يأثره محمد عن مسيلمة (¬14)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p430/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p430/r6.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p430/r6.claim: Al-Kalbi says Muhammad transmitted it from the people of Babylon.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p430/r6.anchor: وقال الكلبي: يأثره عن أهل بابل (¬1) (¬2)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p430/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p430/r7.speaker: الوليد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p430/r7.claim: When Quraysh asked after his reflection, al-Walid told them Muhammad was a sorcerer and his Qur’an was transmitted magic, dividing families.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p430/r7.anchor: قالا (¬3): قال الوليد لقومه لما سألوه عن قوله في محمد بعد ما تفكر ونظر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p430/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p430/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p430/r8.claim: Athara al-hadith originally meant relating something from a people by following their traces after they died; it came to mean narration and reporting generally.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p430/r8.anchor: وهو من قولهم: أثرت الحديث أثرا، إذا حدثت به عن قوم في آثارهم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p430/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p430/r9.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p430/r9.claim: Umar’s expression about neither recalling nor reporting an oath illustrates the extended sense of athara.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p430/r9.anchor: ومنه حديث عمر -رضي الله عنه-: "فما حلفت بها ذاكرا ولا آثرا"

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p430/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p430/r10.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p430/r10.claim: On this reading, the Qur’an is preferred above all magic; yu’thar derives from īthār, preferring one thing.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p430/r10.anchor: وقال عطاء عن ابن عباس: يؤثر على جميع السحر (¬1). وعلى هذا هو من الإيثار.

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p446/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p446/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p446/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that al-Walid heard the Quran and praised its sweet, forceful language as unlike poetry, but after Abu Jahl pressed him to denounce Muhammad he called it transmitted magic; verses 74:11–24 were revealed.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p446/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس: أن الوليد بن المغيرة جاء إلى النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - فقرأ عليه القرآن وكأنه رق له، فبلغ ذلك أبا جهل،

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p447/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p447/r1.speaker: مجاهد
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p447/r1.claim: Mujahid reports al-Walid's deliberation and his eventual charge that the Quran was magic, after rejecting Quraysh's claims that Muhammad was mad, a soothsayer, poet, or liar.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p447/r1.anchor: وقال مجاهد: إن الوليد بن المغيرة كان يغشى النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - وأبا بكر - رضي الله عنه - حتى حسبت قريش أنه يسلم،

STUDYQURAN:74:11/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:74:11/r2.speaker: Ibn ʿAbbās
STUDYQURAN:74:11/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās relates that al-Walīd’s heart softened after hearing the Prophet recite; Abū Jahl pressured him to denounce Muhammad, and al-Walīd praised the Quran’s unlike-poetry, sweet, abundant speech before branding it inherited sorcery, prompting this passage.
STUDYQURAN:74:11/r2.anchor: Ibn ʿAbbās related that al-Walīd went to the Prophet, who recited the Quran to him, and his heart seemed to soften to it

STUDYQURAN:74:11/r25.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:74:11/r25.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:74:11/r25.claim: After considering other ways to disparage Muhammad and the Quran, al-Walīd settled on sorcery as his final judgment; opponents similarly called revelations manifest sorcery.
STUDYQURAN:74:11/r25.anchor: Discounting the other possible ways to denigrate the Prophet and the Quran, al-Walīd

TABATABAI:74:12-25/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:74:12-25/r10.speaker: author
TABATABAI:74:12-25/r10.claim: The sequence portrays al-Walid after deliberation: he looks to judge, frowns and shows disgust, then turns away and grows arrogant before speaking.
TABATABAI:74:12-25/r10.anchor: تمثيل لحاله بعد التكفير والتقدير وهو من ألطف التمثيل وأبلغه

TABATABAI:74:12-25/r14.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:74:12-25/r14.speaker: author
TABATABAI:74:12-25/r14.claim: Calling the Qurʾan ‘transmitted magic’ manifests al-Walid’s rejection and pride; he claims it is learned from sorcerers.
TABATABAI:74:12-25/r14.anchor: أي أظهر إدباره واستكباره بقوله مفرعا عليه { إن هذا } أي القرآن { إلا سحر يؤثر } أي يروى ويتعلم من السحرة

BURSEVI:v10p178/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p178/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p178/r1.claim: He turned from truth, arrogantly refused to follow it, and then spoke.

BURSEVI:v10p178/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p178/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p178/r2.claim: An is a negative particle meaning mā, as shown by the following illā; hādhā refers to the Quran.
BURSEVI:v10p178/r2.anchor: نافية بمعنى ما لذا أورد إلا بعدها

BURSEVI:v10p178/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p178/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p178/r3.claim: The charge is that magic was transmitted and learned from others, not performed by the Prophet; athara originally meant relating what one heard from predecessors, then came to mean transmitting.
BURSEVI:v10p178/r3.anchor: يقال أثرت الحديث آثهر أثرا إذا حدثت به عن قوم في آثارهم

BURSEVI:v10p178/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p178/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p178/r4.claim: Studying magic for a sound purpose is allowed, but believing in its reality and practicing it are disbelief; the cited couplet says knowledge of evil can protect against it.
BURSEVI:v10p178/r4.anchor: وفي تعلم لسحر لحكمة رخصة واعتقاد حقيته والعمل به كفر

TABRISI:74:11-31#2/r25.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:74:11-31#2/r25.speaker: author
TABRISI:74:11-31#2/r25.claim: He claimed that the Qurʾān was magic transmitted from other sorcerers.
TABRISI:74:11-31#2/r25.anchor: فنقول ساحر يؤثر ما أتى به عن غيره من السحرة

TABRISI:74:25-31/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:74:25-31/r1.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:74:25-31/r1.claim: Alternatively, the magic is called transmitted because souls favor and choose it for its sweetness.
TABRISI:74:25-31/r1.anchor: وقيل: هو من الإيثار أي سحر تؤثره النفوس وتختاره لحلاوته فيها

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:74:21-27/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:74:21-27/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:74:21-27/r4.claim: He claimed that Muhammad’s recitation was magic transmitted from sorcerers.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:74:21-27/r4.anchor: { فقال إن هذا } ما هذا الذي يقرؤه محمد { إلا سحر يؤثر } يروى عن السحرة.

ELMALILI:74:14-25/r18.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:74:14-25/r18.speaker: author
ELMALILI:74:14-25/r18.claim: One reading takes the phrase as inherited magic, supposedly taught and passed down from one practitioner to another.
ELMALILI:74:14-25/r18.anchor: yani öteden beri tâlim ve rivayet olunagelen ehlinden ehline öğrenilegeldiği söylenen bir sihir demektir

ELMALILI:74:14-25/r19.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:74:14-25/r19.speaker: author
ELMALILI:74:14-25/r19.claim: Alternatively, yu'thar can mean magic preferred or admired above other magic, with a dazzling, captivating appeal.
ELMALILI:74:14-25/r19.anchor: îsâr olunacak, sâir sihirlere tercih edilecek, beğenilecek bir sihir demek olur

ELMALILI:74:14-25/r21.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:74:14-25/r21.speaker: الوليد بن المغيرة
ELMALILI:74:14-25/r21.claim: In the reported account, al-Walid first praised the Quran's sweetness, beauty, fruitfulness, and incomparable height, but later called it transmitted magic and human speech.
ELMALILI:74:14-25/r21.anchor: Velîd b. Mugīre Peygamber sallallâhu aleyhi ve sellem Hazretleri’nin yanına gelmiş, Kur’an dinlemiş, bir teessür duymuştu

ELMALILI:74:14-25/r22.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:74:14-25/r22.speaker: author
ELMALILI:74:14-25/r22.claim: The account says Quraysh accused al-Walid of straying; Abu Jahl persuaded him to make a public denunciation despite al-Walid's wealth and expertise in poetry.
ELMALILI:74:14-25/r22.anchor: bunu işiten Ebû Cehil “ben size onun hakkından gelirim” deyip

ELMALILI:74:14-25/r23.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:74:14-25/r23.speaker: الوليد بن المغيرة
ELMALILI:74:14-25/r23.claim: Under pressure, al-Walid argued that Muhammad was not insane, a soothsayer, a poet, or a liar, yet produced the verdict of magic and human speech to satisfy the assembly.
ELMALILI:74:14-25/r23.anchor: hiç kimseyi boğarken gördünüz mü? Kâhin diyorsunuz

ELMALILI:74:14-25/r24.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:74:14-25/r24.speaker: author
ELMALILI:74:14-25/r24.claim: The account ends with the assembly applauding al-Walid's denunciation and dispersing.
ELMALILI:74:14-25/r24.anchor: Bunun üzerine hoşlarına gitmiş, meclislerinde bir alkıştır kopmuş, onun sözünü alkışlayarak dağılmışlar

ELMALILI:74:14-25/r25.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:74:14-25/r25.speaker: author
ELMALILI:74:14-25/r25.claim: Some treat the incident as the occasion for the beginnings of al-Muzzammil and al-Muddaththir; Elmalılı says it concerns these verses, since the recited passages were from the Ha-Mims.
ELMALILI:74:14-25/r25.anchor: Velîd’in dinlediği âyetler حٰمٓ’lerden olduğuna dair vâki‘olan rivayetlerden de anlaşıldığına göre bu, bu sûrenin başının değil, bu âyetlerinin sebeb-i nüzûlü olmuştur

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:18/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:18/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:18/r3.claim: Verses 18–25 condemn people who, like al-Walīd, adopt a similar unbelieving posture toward the Qur’an.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:18/r3.anchor: İşte 18-25. âyetlerde Velîd b. Mug^re örneğinde Kur’an’a karşı benzer şekilde inkârcı tutum sergileyenler kınanmış

BURHAN:v2p110/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p110/r7.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p110/r7.claim: The author says pride made al-Walīd recant his recognition and call the Qurʾān transmitted magic and human speech.
BURHAN:v2p110/r7.anchor: ثم حملته الحمية فنكص على عقبيه وكابر حسه

FARRA:v3p202/r3.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p202/r3.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p202/r3.claim: Al-Walid passed Muslims at the Sacred Mosque, called Muhammad a sorcerer whose words came from Musaylima and Babylon, then turned away scowling and arrogant; this explains the transmitted-magic claim.
FARRA:v3p202/r3.anchor: مر على طائفة من المسلمين في المسجد الحرام، فقالوا: هل لك إلى الإسلام يا أبا المغيرة؟

FARRA:v3p202/r4.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p202/r4.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p202/r4.claim: The claim is that Muhammad learned this magic from Babylonian sorcerers.

NAHHAS:v5p67/r7.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p67/r7.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p67/r7.claim: Finding no argument, he disbelieved and then made the following claim.
NAHHAS:v5p67/r7.anchor: لما لم يجد حجة كفر ثم قال

ASAD-NOTES:74:16/r4.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:74:16/r4.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:74:16/r4.claim: He dismisses the revelation as old spellbinding eloquence and calls it the word of a mortal.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p329/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p329/r14.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p329/r14.claim: An unnamed report recounts al-Walid debating Abu Jahl and Quraysh: he praised the Quran's sweetness and force, rejected poetry, soothsaying, and madness, then conceded that it resembled magic; the report circulated in variants with the same gist.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p329/r14.anchor: روي أن الوليد حاج أبا جهل وجماعة من قريش في أمر القرآن وقال: إن له لحلاوة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p269/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p269/r8.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p269/r8.claim: He claimed that what Muhammad recited was only magic transmitted from and attributed to sorcerers.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p269/r8.anchor: {فقال إن هذا} ما هذا الذي يقرؤه محمد {إلا سحر يؤثر} يروى ويحكى عن السحرة.

BAYDAWI-FULL:74:20-28/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:74:20-28/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:74:20-28/r6.claim: He calls it magic that is transmitted or learned; the fa marks his blurting out the phrase as soon as it occurred to him.
BAYDAWI-FULL:74:20-28/r6.anchor: يروى ويتعلم، والفاء للدلالة على أنه لما خطرت هذه الكلمة بباله

DURR-FULL:v8p327/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p327/r11.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v8p327/r11.claim: Qatada recounts that al-Walid considered Muhammad’s words sweet, beautiful, fruitful, and dominant, yet concluded they were magic; the condemnation from how he measured through becoming sullen was revealed about him.
DURR-FULL:v8p327/r11.anchor: عن قتادة {ذرني ومن خلقت وحيدا} قال: هو الوليد بن المغيرة

DURR-FULL:v8p330/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p330/r2.speaker: مجاهد عن ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p330/r2.claim: Mujahid reports Ibn Abbas saying al-Walid canvassed Quraysh’s views, rejected poetry and soothsaying based on his expertise, then reflected and called the message magic passed on from others.
DURR-FULL:v8p330/r2.anchor: من طريق مجاهد عن ابن عباس قال: لما بعث النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم جمع الوليد بن المغيرة قريشا

DURR-FULL:v8p331/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p331/r11.speaker: أبو رزين
DURR-FULL:v8p331/r11.claim: Abu Razin explains “magic transmitted” as magic taken from someone else.
DURR-FULL:v8p331/r11.anchor: عن أبي رزين {إن هذا إلا سحر يؤثر} قال: يأثره عن غيره

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p395/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p395/r1.speaker: أكثر المفسرين
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p395/r1.claim: After pressure, al-Walid rejected poetry, called the Quran transmitted magic and human speech; exegetes explain this as falsely presented as revelation from God.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p395/r1.anchor: أقول هو سحر يؤثر هو قول البشر، أي لبس منزل من عند الله قال أكثر المفسرين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p395/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p395/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p395/r7.claim: يؤثر means narrated or transmitted: al-Walid alleged Muhammad carried the Quran from someone else.

JISHUMI:v10p7156/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7156/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7156/r10.claim: The passage is said to concern al-Walid ibn al-Mughira al-Makhzumi, wealthy with sons and called al-Wahid among his people, according to Ibn Amir.
JISHUMI:v10p7156/r10.anchor: قيل: نزلت هذه الآيات في الوليد بن المغيرة المخزومي، وكان له مال وبنون، قال ابن عامر: وكان يسمى الوحيد في قومه،

JISHUMI:v10p7156/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7156/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7156/r11.claim: In the story, al-Walid rejects calling Muhammad a soothsayer, poet, or madman, then chooses “magician” and says the Qur’an separates families.
JISHUMI:v10p7156/r11.anchor: ثم اختلفوا، فقيل: إنه أتى قريشا في ناديها، وقال: هذا الموسم، والناس يسألون عن محمد،

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p650/r10.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p650/r10.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p650/r10.claim: Al-Walīd first praised the Qur'an's sweetness and grandeur; Abū Jahl drew him back, after which he denied Muhammad was mad, soothsayer, poet, or liar, then called the Qur'an sorcery transmitted from Musaylima and Babylon.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p650/r10.anchor: أن الوليد قال لبني مخزوم : والله لقد سمعت من محمد آنفا

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p651/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p651/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p651/r3.claim: The فاء shows he spoke as soon as the phrase occurred to him.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p651/r3.anchor: لم يتمالك أن نطق بها من غير تلبث

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p651/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p651/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p651/r4.claim: The second accusation is unjoined because it confirms the first.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p651/r4.anchor: من الأولى مجرى التوكيد من المؤكد

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p142/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p142/r8.speaker: ابن زيد
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p142/r8.claim: Ibn Zayd says al-Walid called the Quran transmitted magic, learned by Muhammad from earlier people.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p142/r8.anchor: قال ابن زيد : إن الوليد بن المغيرة قال : إن هذا القرآن إلا سحر يأثره محمد عن غيره فأخذه عمن تقدمه

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p142/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p142/r9.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p142/r9.claim: A further reading is that the Quran affects souls through its sweetness as magic does.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p142/r9.anchor: ويحتمل وجها آخر : أن يكون معناه أن النفوس تؤثر لحلاوته فيها كالسحر .

MUQATIL:74:18-30/r6.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:74:18-30/r6.speaker: author
MUQATIL:74:18-30/r6.claim: Al-Walid turned away arrogantly and called the Qur'an transmitted magic and human speech.
MUQATIL:74:18-30/r6.anchor: { ثم أدبر واستكبر فقال إن هذآ إلا سحر يؤثر إن هذآ إلا قول البشر سأصليه سقر } [آية: 26]
